about.title: Fowler Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Fowler is a small, tight-knit Fresno County community, but that doesn't mean local businesses and property owners get a pass when hazards go unaddressed. Grocery stores, gas stations, and shops along Golden State Boulevard and Manning Avenue see steady foot traffic, and a spilled liquid, cracked pavement, or icy entryway can lead to a serious fall in seconds. California law requires an injured person to show the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the dangerous condition and failed to fix it or warn visitors. That's why documentation matters so much — photos of the hazard, witness names, and store surveillance footage can make or break a claim. If you were hurt on someone else's property in Fowler, LawProactive can connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney experienced in gathering that kind of evidence before it disappears.

whyChoose.title: Why Notice and Evidence Matter in Fowler Falls

items.title: Proving the Owner Knew or Should Have Known
items.desc: California premises liability claims hinge on notice — an attorney can help track down maintenance logs, complaint records, or prior incident reports to establish the property owner was aware of the hazard.

items.title: Preserving Surveillance Before It's Erased
items.desc: Many stores overwrite security footage within days or weeks, so getting a preservation request out quickly is critical to capturing what really happened.

items.title: Understanding Comparative Fault
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you're partly responsible for the fall — an attorney can help make sure your share of fault isn't overstated by the property owner's insurer.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Fowler?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city building or school, that deadline is much shorter and requires an earlier claim filing, so it's worth checking your situation promptly.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my fall?
items.answer: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for the accident. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, rather than barred outright.

items.question: I fell at a business near Golden State Boulevard in Fowler — what should I do first?
items.answer: Try to take photos of exactly what caused the fall, note the time and location, and ask the business to preserve any surveillance footage in writing if you can. Seeking medical attention and reporting the incident to the property manager also helps create a record that supports your claim later.
